recent_reviews.author: Bob Davies
recent_reviews.text: The next patients' group meeting is on the 6th of May at 5pm. We established that patients can arrive a little early (say 10 minutes) to discuss individual problems/experience, so the PPG can focus clearly on shared problems. Whether you can attend or not, please write your review, good or bad, and I will continue to bring them to the new team. From the PPG meeting on Feb 4th... The practice is fully staffed for doctors (now at 6, and 6 admin) but doesn't have a practice manager as they're having trouble recruiting because they will also manage the Oldham practice. I have been assured they're wiring up a better fallback after 2 missed calls (most likely you will receive a text that asks you to ring the practice, but I have asked that a bookable slot picker be added too). The website is now 24hr accessible for admin/repeats, but still cannot be used out of office hours to request an appointment. The doctor has concerns about people using it for 'urgent' requests in the middle of the night (when no doctor is available to receive it), I've tried to make a case for it, but if out of hours appointment-requests is a blocker for you, please come to meetings and help me argue the case. I have also reraised when tests come back all green, but you're still sick, the practice currently close your diagnosis process until you re-engage (which you may not be told you need to do), which I intend to reraise in future. --- From the PPG meeting on November 26th... 2 new doctors are on board, and new staff are coming soon. Complaints about reception seem to be improving, less reliance on agency staff. The website will be switched to 24hr accessible. New Bank is on Bookable, which is much easier to use and is currently accessible outside of office hours (unlike PATCHS), but doesn't work for existing registered patients, and only has a limited number of slots and is only for booking an appointment. --- From the PPG meeting on 10th of September. The practice is moving to a new digital system on 1st of October, which 'should' solve some of the current technical issues with arranging appointments. Management say there will be some onboarding help and open/group sessions for anybody who would like to attend, and dates/times of those will be on a notice-board in the reception (or from Lynne, the operations manager) once those dates are arranged (probably a couple of evenings/saturdays depending on demand). We have also been assurred the quality of help from reception has been better in the last month and will continue to improve. There is still no new practice manager. They are recruiting for one in a difficult market, but they are adding new administrators (from October 6th, if I understood correctly) and _should_ soon be adding extra doctors too, with a less clear timescale (presumably notice-period related). The patient load on doctors is within the normal NHS range, so do not put off making an appointment just because you think they're busy, they have capacity and are adding more, and most of the problems seem to be steadily improving. --- After leaving a previous 1 star review with many negative points and being frustrated with being unable to arrange an appointment, I attended the newly set-up Patient Participation Group meeting (as a new management company took over in April) on 6th August. The discussion between the team and a few patients was constructive and the new management team seem to have an understanding of the problems after we explained in some detail. I also brought these reviews to their attention, and provided a breakdown of reviews to their management in the meeting. If you're here because you've had a negative experience, either recently or before the take-over, we've been assured they're working on it and should be moving to a new system, as well as dealing with the problems caused by specific staff. Please contact management with feedback and come to the patient meeting if you have the time, be heard, the new team are (it seems) finally listening, and they actually have a mandate to fix problems atm.

recent_reviews.author: Ken Kamdy
recent_reviews.text: A call was initiated to ascertain why an appointment for a mother and child was declined by a GP, providing clinical advice to the service user, and you are not part of the medical team. NHS staff must not unreasonably deny access to services, and patients are entitled to be treated with dignity, receive clear information, and file a formal complaint regarding inadequate care or discourteous conduct. However, a staff member and a receptionist unjustly canceled an appointment, and I have requested the call log. Non-clinical reception staff should not act as if they are GPs; clinical decisions regarding whether a baby or parent requires a review should be made by a qualified health professional (GP, nurse, ANP) following appropriate triage protocols. Professional guidance underscores that healthcare professionals must not unreasonably refuse a patient access to care that addresses their needs and must communicate with kindness and clarity, particularly with vulnerable patients such as parents of very young children. A receptionist informing a practice or service user that she does not consult a GP also provides clinical advice to the service user. Merely asserting that a one-year-old “does not need to see a GP” without a proper clinical evaluation or justification is unlikely to adhere to good practice standards regarding communication and access to care. It is unfortunate that this matter is not being addressed; I intend to escalate this issue further due to the appalling service.

recent_reviews.author: Fiona Simpson
recent_reviews.text: I am always really happy with and satisfied with all interactions with the surgery, and actually recommend it to others. The 2 main doctors and advanced clinician are always very good and are through, listen and take concerns seriously. The patches system is very good and easy to use - myself and spouse have had to use it a few times recently, and we have always then been contacted with an appropriate appointment, if that was face to face, urgent phone, or routine that has always happened quickly. There are some people complaining about lack of appointments etc, I have never found this to be the case. I work in primary care and regularly deal with different GP surgeries, and believe me, simpson medical are one of the better ones!! Perhaps everyone needs to have realistic expectations, and consider that there is high demand for healthcare, which exceeds capacity. The old days of face to face appointments are gone, unless it is necessary this does not happen anymore - often phone calls, including photos etc are often sufficent, and more a more efficient use of staff resources. If a face to face appointment is necessary it will be made whilst anything regarding mental health has always been taking seriously and urgently. I am very happy with being a patient here, and think given the demand they do a good job, and are one of the better surgeries I deal with. Thank you to the staff, I appreciate it

recent_reviews.author: Junaid Ahmed
recent_reviews.text: As a long-term patient (diagnosed with a life time illness since 2005) receiving continuous prescriptions and specialized care, I requested a paid private letter confirming the simple, medically accepted fact that chronic stress and hardship trigger flare-ups to my condition. The practice refused the request, claiming "insufficient evidence" a shocking statement considering my two decades as a patient for whom they have continuously prescribed, medication, are informed of my hospital ongoing treatment for years (Vedolizumab, etc.) and liaised with the hospital IBD team. This refusal demonstrates a failure to understand the patient they are treating. Crucially, this contradiction occurred even though I attached an older letter from my specialist consultant where this clinical fact was already written and acknowledged. This extreme administrative obstacle wasted significant time and energy, forcing me to change GPs due to their unwillingness to support a chronic patient.

recent_reviews.author: JUNAID AHMED
recent_reviews.text: I was a long-term patient with multiple chronic conditions, including ulcerative colitis, arthritis, and migraines — all of which were regularly managed through prescriptions and hospital treatments. I requested a simple private letter confirming my diagnosis and how stress can affect my condition — something a hospital consultant had previously provided. Despite being willing to pay the £35 fee, the practice refused to provide the letter and didn’t offer an appointment to discuss it. As someone managing serious long-term health issues, I found this response dismissive and lacking in basic patient support. I’ve since moved to a new GP who I hope will be more patient-focused. I’m sharing this to help others understand what kind of support they might — or might not — receive here if they have complex or ongoing health needs. To the management: the decline in care became noticeable after COVID. If you’re genuinely reviewing patient experiences, it may be worth examining the internal changes made during and after the pandemic — because that’s when the ship started sinking.

recent_reviews.author: Hamaad Farooq
recent_reviews.text: I visited the surgery today while in severe pain and was told my prescription would be sent to the pharmacy. I went to the pharmacy but the prescription had not been sent. I returned after one hour and it was still not there. When I called the surgery, the receptionist told me to wait another hour while they checked with the doctor. When someone is in severe pain and unable to drive, delays like this are extremely frustrating and unacceptable. The doctor was kind and helpful, but the communication and urgency from reception staff needs serious improvement. What is also frustrating is that when staff are rude it seems to be accepted, but when a patient in severe pain becomes frustrated it is quickly labelled as “abuse.” Patients deserve to be treated with understanding and respect, especially when they are in pain and asking for urgent help.

recent_reviews.author: Philip Crossley
recent_reviews.text: Lottery appointment system, You need to call between 8am to 8:30am to win a appointment, but everyone else is also calling at the same time. If your call actually connects during this period, congratulations you have a ticket that gets you a 30% chance of an appointment ( providing they have not all been taken already) , if not try the lottery again the next day. You have 1/5 chance for an appointment if you follow my advice. I have a hack for those needing urgent doctor, use all the phones you can get access to and call them one after another, one will likely get through. Edit: It is possible now to go into the doctors before 8 am to obtain a golden ( yellow ) ticket, which helps you bypass the lottery phone system and be seen the same day. While the lottery system is not ideal, I can see its a way to deal with a already struggling health system and therefore I am rating this place higher for finding a way to deal with a failing system. (+2 stars )

recent_reviews.text: Dear Practice Manager, I am writing to make a formal complaint regarding the conduct of a receptionist during my calls to the surgery on 22/09/2025 at approximately 08:30am. During the call, I provided my son’s date of birth correctly ( date birth ). The receptionist repeatedly insisted that I had given the wrong date, despite me clarifying several times. This interaction became unnecessarily argumentative, and instead of acknowledging my clarification, she accused me of raising my voice, which was not the case. Feeling distressed, I called back and asked for my call to be transferred to another colleague who might better understand the situation. The same receptionist refused to transfer the call, insisting she had already corrected the date, which I found unacceptable and unprofessional. This is not the first time I have experienced rudeness from this particular staff member. As a parent of a young child, I expect to be treated with respect and professionalism when contacting the surgery, especially when the matter concerns my child’s health. I kindly request that this incident be investigated, that appropriate action be taken to address the receptionist’s behaviour, and that I receive a written response regarding the outcome of my complaint. Thank you for your attention to this matter. Sincerely and I will make this formal 100%

I am very grateful for the care and support he provided to my family.

recent_reviews.author: Faiz ul Haq
recent_reviews.text: I would like to leave negative feedback regarding Dr. Hussain’s behavior at this surgery. Whenever we ask him for medicine, even for our small children, he always responds by saying: “Go and pick it up from the shelf.” Most recently, my wife, who is pregnant, needed medicine. Whenever she calls, despite the language barrier, Dr. Hussain should at least try to understand that a patient is in need of proper medical advice and prescriptions. Instead, he simply tells her to “get it from the shelf.” I want to ask: if we always have to buy medicine directly from the shelf, then what is the point of having a doctor or a surgery? What role is he fulfilling? During the last call, my wife explained that the medicine he had prescribed previously did not help her at all. She requested an alternative. Instead of listening, Dr. Hussain told her she must not be using the medicine properly. My wife clearly said she knows how to take it, but it was ineffective. At that point, Dr. Hussain disconnected the call and again told her to “buy it from the shelf.” This behavior is extremely unprofessional, dismissive, and rude—especially towards a pregnant woman and parents with small children. A doctor should listen carefully, show empathy, and provide proper medical guidance. Unfortunately, Dr. Hussain’s attitude shows the opposite. I strongly believe that this kind of conduct is unacceptable within the NHS. If doctors are not willing to provide proper medical care and instead simply tell patients to “buy from the shelf,” then they are not fulfilling their responsibility as healthcare providers. I will also be submitting a formal complaint to the NHS regarding this matter. In my opinion, Dr. Hussain should consider retirement, as he does not treat patients with the respect, care, and professionalism that is expected from a doctor.

recent_reviews.author: Honey
recent_reviews.text: Awful experience this morning at this practice. First of all they thought the best time to do a fire drill would be with a full waiting room and in the freezing cold and rain. Then when we came inside which was 10 minutes after my appointment was meant to be I checked my nhs app to see that my appointment had been changed to 10:45 without my knowledge or notification. There was a reason I booked it at 10:20 not 10:45. I have also never experienced this in the past but I assume it’s so they meet their key performance metrics around access and availability. Some clarity on this would be good and do not blame the fire drill as it was nearly 10 after I should’ve had my appointment when the fire drill was done. Then the nurse I saw basically just fobbed me off when my condition hasn’t improved at all in a week. I have been told to wait another week and come back if it doesn’t improve despite already waiting before I came in to see someone in the first place.

Furthermore, my condition I've been visiting about causes me unbearable pain which the practice won't even prescribe pain killers for.Like Share Response from the owner a month agoDear Sydney Thank you for taking the time to provide feedback regarding your recent experience at the practice. I am sorry to hear about the distress and frustration this caused you and appreciate the opportunity to respond. My name is Lesley Hyde and I am the Practice Business Manager and part of my role is to monitor and investigate any concerns or complaints made to the practice. Please se below my response to the issues you have raised: Sample Collection Arrangements We apologise for the inconvenience caused when you attended the practice to drop off a sample at 6pm and were advised that it could not be accepted at that time. We understand how frustrating this must have been for you. For clarity, samples must be received by the practice by 4:00pm to ensure they can be included in the scheduled daily laboratory collection at 4:30pm. Samples received after this time cannot be accepted, as they may not be stored within the required conditions and timeframes set by the laboratory. Accepting samples outside of these parameters risks inaccurate or invalid results, which could affect patient care and safety. We do have a poster displayed in our reception area outlining the sample cut off time; however, we acknowledge your feedback that this information may not have been sufficiently visible prior to your visit. As a result of your comments, we have now placed additional signage on our front entrance door and updated our practice website to make sample submission times clearer and more accessible. You can view this update here: https://www.thearchmedicalpractice.co.uk/practice-information/sample-collection/ Our clinicians usually advise patients of the relevant sample drop off times when issuing sample pots. If this did not occur in your case, we sincerely apologise. We have reminded all clinical and reception staff of the importance of clearly communicating sample cut-off times to patients to help prevent similar situations in the future. Access to the Practice Building We are sorry that you felt unable to re-enter the practice and that this added to your distress. For staff safety reasons, when a receptionist is working alone at the front desk and their colleague is temporarily required elsewhere, the front door may be placed on a buzzer system. In these circumstances, patients are still able to gain access by pressing the buzzer and would be let in by a member of staff. We regret if this was not clear at the time and if it appeared that the practice was closed earlier than advertised. I can assure you however, the practice was still open. Pain Management and Ongoing Care We are sorry to hear about the level of pain you are experiencing. Prescribing decisions, including pain relief, are made by clinicians based on individual clinical assessment and current medical guidance to ensure patient safety. A GP would only prescribe “pain killers” if they felt there was a clinical indication to do so. If your symptoms are persisting, then I would encourage you to arrange a further appointment with a clinician so that your pain and ongoing symptoms can be reviewed again. Next Steps We take all feedback seriously and are grateful that you have brought these matters to our attention, which has already led to improvements in how we share information with patients. If you would like your concerns to be investigated further under the NHS complaints procedure, or if you wish to discuss my response further, please contact me at the practice (0161 226 0606). We are always looking for new members to join our PPG, if you would like further information of if you are interested in joining is, please click the below link: https://www.thearchmedicalpractice.co.uk/practice-information/patient-participation-group/ Yours faithfully Mrs Lesley Hyde Practice Business Manager

recent_reviews.author: Liv Zachariasen
recent_reviews.text: Keep dismissing me when I contact them when my toddler is poorly They just refer me to a pharmacy that I can't get to. If I want my toddler to be seen, I have to put through a complaint as it's the only way they'll take me seriously and the last time he turned out to have tonsilitis. My requests on AskmyGP just get closed off with a link to a pharmacy. I was never informed I'd have to be seen by a pharmacy first when I registered at this practice and it has never been communicated. They claim you'll be seen sooner, but before this we've always been sble to be seen on the day. I will never understand fobbing off parents who are worried about their small children and I get this every single time now. I have to always push to be seen and when they finally agree, I'm already so upset and stressed by the whole dismissiveness that I can't be bothered speaking to them. Not sure contacting a GP is supposed to trigger anxiety? It's more than reasonable to not rely on a pharmacy for diagnosis, especially for small children!! The last time he had a fever I didn't even bother contacting them as I couldn't be bothered with the thought of being fobbed off with a pharmacy referral. I get that the NHS is stretched and particularly GP practices, but you should be allowed a consultation every once in a while without a battle. I definitely hope nothing serious ever happens to myself or my family or we better hope the pharmacy can treat us. However having seen the pharmacist as they told me to, I'm none the wiser so what an absolute waste of people's time and energy to pass them round such a useless and inefficient circus. So disappointed as they have resorted to such a lazy way of dealing with their patients.

recent_reviews.text: Awful experience. Taken me off the database because I’ve moved from the area, even though I work 5 minutes away. I expressed that I would struggle changing gps because of underlying issues and they didn’t show any empathy. I expressed that my dentist etc were still in Manchester, as I am physically unavailable through the week to attend any appointments, working 6am until 8pm Monday to Friday. I stated that I’d had an ongoing condition, knew what it was but they had to test me. The first test they lost, the 2nd test they tested for the incorrect issue, the third they said I didn’t have what I thought. When I was referred to a specialist they confirmed on the day (within minutes of being tested) that I did in fact have what I initially thought! I believe if she wasn’t as strong as she was, just may have tried something unthinkable. When I sent a letter of complaint nothing was done. The doctors name is Dr Hoddes! They misdiagnose people, give them antibiotics or painkillers and they end up dying of cancer. Avoid at all costs!!!

recent_reviews.author: Oj B
recent_reviews.text: It's so heartbreaking to see this practice degenerate to this level. How hard can it be for people to be nice and professional? They have a lot to do in terms of training all their staff. And I mean ALL of them! From people's skills to civility, mannerisms, tone of voice when addressing patients and how to approach to patients who are already suffering. I've had so many unpleasant encounters with them that I don't want to mention. They make it look like they are doing a favour by attending to you. So appalling! They soon will be having no stars whatsoever if they don't make proper and needed adjustments on their people's skills. It really is appalling! Yelling at patients!! 9/03/2026 I can't believe that I am back here after 4 years to leave a very negative review of this establishment. Before, I go any further - I want to make it clear that, whatever issues patients are having with this medical centre are 90 to 95% front desk, admin, nurses and lesser staff (sorry, for lack of a better word to use.) The Dr's are unaware of the front desk, admin, and lesser staff issues - and yet bear the brunt of the end of the stick should the establishment suffer. I've had very unbelievable and excrutiatingly painful experiences with them from the beginning of this year. In short, (they put up lies and mark your profile, including your number should you call and then mete you undeserved shabby treatment by whoever picks your call, and for whatever reasons best known to them). From the tone of answering your call and how you are responded to is clear and obvious! It is like a syndicate in operation!!! Very evil and unprofessional!!! But we must continue to voice these issues until changes are made, and wrongs are righted. This afternoon I made a call to the centre, having moved to a new home, my daughter who had ran out of medication, due to pressure of moving into a new home and the process of registering with a near gp when settled; called Gorton Medical centre before the weekend to kindly ask for a repeat to be sent to the pharmacy for her to collect. It was not actioned. We called 111 for emergency prescription over the weekend. Today being Monday and on her last tablet, I called the pharmacy to ask if her prescription has come through from the gp, and they said it hadn't. I then called this medical centre to ask why my daughter's prescription had not been actioned and sent to the pharmacy since last week - Knowing she's been on same medication for several years and should not miss days? I was bluntly told by the reception to call back again,(of course, profile marking and syndicate operations in action.) I quickly reminded him how important her medication was, and he should please send it over to the pharmacy for collection. He said he was not in charge of that, and ended up pretending not to understand which medication was needed, (She's only on 1) and is in her profile. To cut the story short, I had no choice but to call 111 again. "Profile marking or spewed lies on the profile" was highly resonant in the voice at the end of the receiver too. I want to clearly state that these issues should be looked into by the right bodies in charge. People are being abused by those that should be providing care, and lives are lost due to these. (I nearly would have lost my life with this centre, cause i was refused care and gp appointment, and was bluntly told to do the worse I can not too long ago.) My daughter was refused duty of care, when she needed, and the excuse was, we had moved homes and was removed by the gp from their system- even when we had not yet registered with another gp. Where is the duty of care? What is the professionalism in this? This is gross misconduct and should be called out. And like I said in the beginning, Dr's are in consulting rooms doing their best and in very high cases are unaware of what goes on at the front desks, admins, and the rest. This types of evil must be called out and put away and far, please.

recent_reviews.author: Gavin Manchester
recent_reviews.text: Unwilling to make reasonable adjustments (due to learning disability) despite the Equality Act 2010 and The Autism Act 2009. Not a suitable surgery for neurodivergent adults (ADHD/autism) with long term lifelong mental health conditions or/and learning disability, not unless you have a parent/family friend to speak on your behalf, book and accompany you to appointments. Admin staff not understanding or particularly helpful and hold grudges/make assumptions, no training in autism/learning disability. (Even if the patient is on the NHS Learning Disability Register). On one occasion I had a local authority social worker attend an appointment with me as an advocate and to see the challenges I face accessing lawful care. Complain or raise concerns and get told “go elsewhere”. Not a particularly modern thinking practice. Very much the “you don’t look autistic” attitude and “go for a long walk outdoors” when facing a serious MH relapse/crisis. Seem to have the attitude that anything mental health related means you must see the CMHT only and if not under psychiatric care they won’t help you. They don’t feel the need to update medical records despite communication from medical consultants. No excuse for treating vulnerable patients so ineffectually or cruelly.

recent_reviews.author: Rose Carbone
recent_reviews.text: Dr Atherton was absolutely great - as always - however it’s the whole booking/reception where there seems to be difficulty & errors - this last apptmt was at least the 3rd time where I’d been given incorrect information. This time it was an error in phone apptmt/face to face apptmt. Id been told it was a phone apptmt - whereas in fact it was supposed to be a face to face one - so I was waiting by the phone at home & no call came. One before I’d been given the wrong month info - so when I turned up at the surgery - my date & time was right but for the wrong month. Prior to that I’d been given a date and time but just before the booked apptmt I received a message from the surgery to tell me I couldn't actually have that apptmt as it had been booked in incorrectly & had been given an ‘emergency’ slot as opposed to routine - I had booked it 3 wks in advance - so then had to wait a further 3/4 weeks to finally speak to a doctor. Like I said when you do manage to speak with a doctor/nurse at the Practice they are brilliant - however some of the booking/reception team do let it down & it becomes very frustrating - especially if you are concerned about an issue. There were further errors - in a similar area but I have bored myself with this already - I’m only writing this because I was asked to & also hope that it can lead to an improvement in the booking system.

recent_reviews.author: The 5 Brothers Squad
recent_reviews.text: Benchill Medical Centre is no longer the practice it used to be. All the old doctors are gone, and what’s left is a team that seems to have no urgency, no compassion, and no sense of responsibility. My 12-year-old son developed a serious issue with his eye — it was clearly getting worse — and we spent over two weeks trying to get him seen. I called multiple times, explained that his condition was deteriorating, and still we were ignored. When they finally responded, they didn’t even book an appointment — they just sent us to a pharmacy, where we received no help at all. This isn’t just poor service — this is gross negligence. They failed to provide proper medical care for a child in pain, and they didn’t even follow up. The delay has made things worse, and we’ve had to seek help elsewhere. No examination, no urgency, no care. This practice has changed for the worse — it is now unsafe and unreliable. If you value your family’s health, especially your children’s, I strongly advise you to go elsewhere.

recent_reviews.author: Amrit Kaur Swalley
recent_reviews.text: During my call, I was advised by reception staff that I should take my mother to the dental hospital instead. This advice appeared to be a medical decision, which I found concerning, as reception staff are not clinically qualified to make such determinations. I later spoke with the reception manager, who confirmed that reception staff are permitted to make these decisions. This is unacceptable and raises serious concerns about patient safety and appropriate triage procedures. In addition, I do not feel that my complaint was handled effectively or taken seriously. There was no reassurance, clear explanation, or appropriate escalation of my concerns. I believe further training is required for reception staff, particularly regarding the limits of their role and the importance of not making or influencing medical decisions. As a patient, I expect clinical advice to be given by a qualified healthcare professional. This matter is particularly concerning given the Care Quality Commission (CQC) requirements, which state that patients must be treated safely, appropriately, and with clear clinical oversight. I trust that this issue will be reviewed promptly to ensure patients are not placed at risk in the future. Thank you

recent_reviews.author: Erandi Samaraweera
recent_reviews.text: ⚠️ Serious patient safety concerns – I strongly advise de-registering I am writing this review as both a medical doctor and a parent who has been genuinely fearful for their child’s safety while registered at Junction Surgery and Alkrington Surgery. Since registering in August 2025, I have experienced repeated safety and professionalism concerns. My child was once prescribed antibiotics without enough doses to complete the course and I was told that “missing a few doses won’t matter.” This is unsafe advice and only corrected after I insisted. My daughter had a persistent cough for several months and attended multiple times, yet no appropriate referral or timely investigations were arranged. When she later developed fever and blood-stained sputum, an out-of-hours GP was clearly concerned and requested urgent investigations. Despite this, our concerns were dismissed the following day, my child was not properly examined, and I was given incorrect medical information. False reassurance when a child is coughing up blood is unacceptable. When I later requested an urgent private ENT referral due to ongoing bleeding, I was asked to pay a fee during a highly distressing situation, despite previously being told such referrals were not chargeable. The supervising GP did not attend to assess my child in person. Overall, I felt unheard, disrespected, and unsafe. Based on my experience, I would strongly advise patients—especially parents of young children—to seriously consider de-registering and seeking care elsewhere. IF ANYONE NOT TRUSTING ME PLEASE READ THE REVIEWS IN OTHER WEBSITE AND CQC REPORT

recent_reviews.author: Xelona Eab
recent_reviews.text: I have been going to this surgery for about 24 years, I had mixed service from Dr Anglin, but have had good treatment from Dr Lazin. I'm pleased Dr Anglin retired he never paid attention to hospital letters sent to him. Dr Lazin is consistent in his care, reads all hospital letters and will correct my repeat prescriptions with new medication without my input, and will change them if they become incorrect, by a telephone call alone. The building is not very wheelchair friendly for chairs with wider seats. I'm pretty sure children or smaller wheelchair users should be able to get through the doors. But my larger chair can't get through any internal doors, so I would be unable to evaluate the building if a fire occured.
